subtopics.title: Mission and Orbit Basics
subtopics.summary: Skyroot Aerospace of Hyderabad launched Vikram-1 on Mission Aagaman, its maiden flight, from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota. The flight placed payloads into Low Earth Orbit and made India the third country, after the US and China, to demonstrate private orbital launch capability. The booklet also separates sub-orbital rockets, which do not place a satellite into orbit, from orbital rockets, which do.
facts: Vikram-1 is India's first privately built orbital launch vehicle.
Maiden flight was Mission Aagaman, launched from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.
The flight placed payloads into Low Earth Orbit.
India became the 3rd country, after US and China, to demonstrate private orbital launch capability.
Vikram-1 is a 4-stage orbital launch vehicle.
The mission was authorised and facilitated by IN-SPACe.
Vikram-1 is named after Dr Vikram Sarabhai, father of India's space programme.
A sub-orbital rocket goes to space but does not place a satellite into orbit.
An orbital rocket places a satellite into orbit around the Earth.
Low Earth Orbit lies between 160 km and 2,000 km above Earth's surface.

subtopics.title: Propulsion and Structure
subtopics.summary: The first three stages of Vikram-1, called Kalam Engines, use advanced solid propellants. The upper stage uses a 3D-printed liquid-fuelled Raman Engine for precise orbital insertion and manoeuvres. The rocket extensively uses all-carbon composite structures, and the booklet also highlights Agnilet, a single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.
facts: Stages 1 to 3 of Vikram-1 are called Kalam Engines.
The Kalam Engines use advanced solid propellants.
The upper stage features a 3D-printed liquid-fuelled Raman Engine.
The Raman Engine is used for precise orbital insertion and manoeuvres.
Vikram-1 extensively uses all-carbon composite structures.
Agnilet is the world's first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.
Agnibaan SOrTeD is the world's first rocket with a fully 3D-printed engine.
SOrTeD stands for SubOrbital Technology Demonstrator.

subtopics.title: Payloads on Board
subtopics.summary: Vikram-1 carries scientific, technological, commercial and symbolic payloads. SCOPE, developed by Skyroot Aerospace, validates onboard spacecraft systems and mission technologies during flight. The Embrace robotic arm, created by Cosmoserve Space, is linked to future applications such as space debris removal and in-orbit servicing.
facts: Vikram-1 carries scientific, technological, commercial and symbolic payloads.
SCOPE, developed by Skyroot Aerospace, validates onboard spacecraft systems and mission technologies during flight.
The Embrace robotic arm, created by Cosmoserve Space, stays attached to the payload deck during its demonstration.
Embrace is linked to future applications such as space debris removal and in-orbit servicing.
SOLARAS is an indigenous CubeSat that demonstrates indigenous satellite technology in orbit.
Cosmic Bloom is India's first lab-grown diamond jewellery sent into space, developed by Cosmos Diamonds.
An 18K gold rocket model carries micro-sculptures of Sir C.V. Raman, Dr Vikram Sarabhai and Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
The gold rocket model is credited to Telangana-based artist Ajay Kumar Mattewada.

subtopics.title: Policy, Regulators and FDI
subtopics.summary: Indian Space Policy 2023 opened the complete space value chain to non-government entities. IN-SPACe works as the single-window regulator for private space activities, while NewSpace India Limited serves as ISRO's commercial arm. FDI limits are set separately for each segment of the space sector.
facts: Indian Space Policy 2023 opened the complete space value chain to non-government entities.
NewSpace India Limited serves as ISRO's commercial arm and was established in 2019.
IN-SPACe functions as a single-window regulator for private space activities.
IN-SPACe stands for Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre and is headquartered in Ahmedabad.
IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme provides grants up to Rs 1 crore to startups and MSMEs.
Antrix Corporation (1992) is the marketing arm of ISRO.
FDI: 74% automatic in satellite manufacturing and operations.
FDI: 49% automatic in launch vehicles and spaceports.
FDI: 100% in satellite components and subsystems.
